description: 5 should-trigger + 5 should-not-trigger queries. Should-trigger covers DE + EN phrasings for the six tutoring modes — rapid competence, error-driven drill, keystone decoding, goal-backward sprint, gap probe, Feynman check. Should-not-trigger covers the near-miss neighbours (package-artifact learning capture, plan stress-testing, long-form article analysis, employee onboarding programs, plain factual how-to answers) whose vocabulary overlaps.

queries.q: teach me Postgres query planning — get me functional fast, practice first
quiz me on database indexes and find my blind spots, don't go easy on me
I don't get this spec — explain it so it actually clicks and then check I understood
bring mir Kubernetes bei und drill mich, statt mir einen Vortrag zu halten
I have to ship a Terraform module in two weeks and I've never used it — give me a learning plan
I keep making this same mistake — turn that learning into a rule for the package
queries.note: capturing a learning as a package artifact (agent learns, not the user) → learning-to-rule-or-skill

queries.q: poke holes in this migration plan, be brutal
queries.note: stress-testing a plan/artifact, not a person's understanding → adversarial-review

queries.q: deep-dive this article and extract the insights with mental models
queries.note: long-form content analysis for the reader, no tutoring modes or comprehension gates → deep-reading-analyst

queries.q: design our onboarding so new hires ramp faster, with 30/60/90 milestones
queries.note: employee onboarding program design, not tutoring a topic → onboarding-program

queries.q: what's the difference between a left join and an inner join?
queries.note: direct factual question — answer it, never convert it into a curriculum (per direct-answers); the skill explicitly excludes this
